evidence_points: The official UKHSA page provides information on cyclohexane for use when responding to chemical incidents.
The page is published by the UK Health Security Agency on GOV.UK.
The publication was first published on 1 July 2014.
The GOV.UK record shows a latest update of 17 February 2025.
The publication provides general information and incident management material.
The linked material supports substance-specific assessment of health effects, exposure and incident response for cyclohexane.
Cyclohexane is also known as hexahydrobenzene, hexamethylene, hexanaphthene and related synonyms.
The official page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026 and retained the title “Cyclohexane: properties and incident management”.
An alert, symptom, exposure report, incident notification or checklist alone does not establish that every recommendation on Cyclohexane: properties and incident management applies.

Final decisions require the current official page scope plus the exact substance, exposure route, concentration or quantity, duration, affected people, setting, measurements, clinical and operational evidence, responsible organisations, protective actions, communication, documentation and review.
